topic.title: Causal Identification with Incomplete Knowledge
topic.overview: Causal identification asks whether available data and assumptions determine the effect of an intervention or a counterfactual outcome. These papers study situations where the full causal graph is unknown, different datasets observe different variables, or only bounds on an answer are possible. Graphical equivalence, conditional independence, and do-calculus provide ways to distinguish what is identifiable from what remains ambiguous.
topic.whyItMatters: A predictive association alone cannot justify a policy intervention. Identification tells analysts which additional assumptions or experiments are needed before estimating an effect, and can expose several valid estimators for the same quantity.
topic.evolution: The collection spans early causal-modeling work from 1987 onward. Recent representatives emphasize conditional effects under graph uncertainty, partial counterfactual identification, and testable adjustments with limited structural knowledge. The 2026 derivation-graph work organizes equivalent causal expressions to support more efficient estimation.
openQuestions: How can identification procedures communicate sensitivity to uncertain structural assumptions?
Which limited experiments most effectively narrow an unresolved causal query?
